question: A Rhumb Line is:

options.text: a line that crosses lines of latitude at a constant angle.
a line that crosses meridians at a constant angle.
a line that crosses the equator at a constant angle.

explanation: A rhumb line (loxodrome) cuts every meridian at the same angle — it is a line of constant true direction.

question: How many nm are equivalent to 1° of arc of latitude:
explanation: 1° of latitude = 60 minutes of arc = 60 NM (1 NM = 1 minute of great-circle arc).

question: The maximum difference between geocentric and geodetic latitude occurs at about:
explanation: Geocentric and geodetic latitude are equal at the Equator and the poles; the difference (≈ 11.6′) is greatest around 45°.

question: The departure between positions 60° N 160° E and 60sN x is 900 NM. What is the longitude of x?
explanation: Departure = d.long(′) × cos lat → 900 = d.long × 0.5 → d.long = 1 800′ = 30°. 160°E + 30° = 190°E = 170°W.

question: Waypoint 1 is 60N 30W. Waypoint 2 is 60N 20W. The aircraft autopilot is coupled to the INS steer. What is the latitude on passing 25 W?
explanation: The great circle between two points on the same parallel bulges towards the pole; its vertex is at the mid-longitude (25°W). tan(lat V) = tan 60° / cos 5° → lat ≈ 60°05.7′N.

question: An inertial navigation system is used to navigate from waypoint 1 (45° N 030° W) to waypoint 2 (45° N 020° W). The distance flown will be:
explanation: An INS flies the great circle. Rhumb-line distance along 45°N = 600′ × cos 45° = 424.26 NM, and the great circle is always shorter → less than 424.25 NM.

question: A great circle is defined as:

options.text: A circle in any plane on the surface of a sphere.
A circle on the surface of a sphere, whose plane is cutting through the centre of the sphere.
A circle running on the outside of the sphere.
A circle on the surface of the sphere, with its plane running perpendicular to the axis of rotation.

explanation: A great circle is the intersection of the sphere with a plane through its centre.

question: Position A is at latitude 33º 45N and position B is at latitude 14º 25N. What is the change in latitude between A and B?
A is at 5500N 15100W and B at 4500 N 16253W What is the departure?
What is the longitude of a position 6 NM to the east of 58° 42N 094° 00W?
explanation: D.long = departure / cos lat = 6 / cos 58°42′ ≈ 11.5′. Moving east from 094°00′W: 093°48.5′W.

question: An aircraft departing A(N40º 00´ E080º 00´ ) flies a constant true track of 270º at a ground speed of 120 kt. What are the coordinates of the position reached in 6 HR?
You fly from 49N to 58N along the 180 E/W meridian. What is the distance in kilometres?
The shortest distance between 2 point of the surface of the earth is:

options.text: the arc of a great circle

explanation: The shortest path between two points on a sphere is the shorter arc of the great circle through them.

question: The automatic flight control system is coupled to the guidance outputs from an inertial navigation system. Which pair of latitudes will give the greatest difference between initial track read-out and the average true course given, in each case, a difference of longitude of 10° ?
explanation: Initial track differs from the mean course by half the convergency = ½ × d.long × sin(mean lat). Largest sin(mean lat) wins: 60°N to 60°N.

question: The Earth has been charted using:
explanation: ICAO requires coordinates referenced to the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS-84).

question: An IRS is programmed with waypoint 1: N60° 00 W030° 00, waypoint 2: N60° 00 W020° 00, waypoint 3: N60° 00 W010° 00. As the aircraft passes waypoint 2 its track will:
explanation: The great-circle leg WP1→WP2 arrives with track 090 + 4.3°; the next leg leaves at 090 − 4.3°. Track decreases by the full convergency 10 × sin 60° ≈ 9°.

question: Consider the following statements on meridians:

options.text: All meridians run in true direction from South to North.
The relative direction between two selected meridians will be constant.
On the southern hemisphere the meridians run towards the south pole.
The distance, in nautical miles, between two selected meridians will be constant.

explanation: Every meridian is a semi-great circle running true north–south from pole to pole.

question: Convergence is:

options.text: the angle of inclination of one parallel of latitude with another.
the angular change of direction of a Rhumb Line course as it passes one meridian to another.
the angle at which a meridian cuts the Equator.
the angle of inclination of meridians towards each other.

explanation: Convergency is the angle of inclination between two meridians (the change in great-circle direction between them).

question: The circumference of the Earth is approximately:
Given that: A is N55 E/W 000 B is N54 E 010 If the true great circle track from A to B is 100T, what is the true Rhumb Line track at A?
explanation: Convergency = 10° × sin 54.5° ≈ 8.1°; conversion angle ≈ 4°. In the northern hemisphere the great circle lies on the polar side of the rhumb line, so eastbound GC track < RL track: RL = 100 + 4 = 104°.

question: What is the initial great circle direction from 45° N 14° 12W to 45° N 12° 48E?
explanation: D.long 27° along 45°N. Initial GC track = 090 − ½ × 27 × sin 45° ≈ 090 − 9.5 = 080.5°T.

question: An aircraft is flying around the Earth eastwards along the 60N parallel of latitude at a groundspeed of 240 knots. At what groundspeed would another aircraft have to fly eastwards along the Equator to fly once round the Earth in the same journey time?
explanation: The 60° parallel is half the length of the Equator (cos 60° = 0.5). Same journey time requires twice the speed: 480 kt.

question: What is the convergence given that two meridians at latitude 60º are 40º apart:
explanation: Convergency = d.long × sin lat = 40 × sin 60° ≈ 34.64°.

question: At what approximate latitude is the length of one minute of arc along a meridian equal to one NM (1852 m) correct?
explanation: Because the Earth is flattened, one minute of latitude varies from ≈ 1 843 m (Equator) to ≈ 1 862 m (poles); it equals 1 852 m at about 45°.

question: You are flying from A (50N 10W) to B (58N 02E). What is the Convergency between A and B?
explanation: Convergency = d.long × sin mean lat = 12 × sin 54° ≈ 9.7°.

question: What is the final position after the following rhumb line tracks and distances have been followed from position 60° 00N 030° 00W? South for 3600 NM East for 3600 NM North for 3600 NM West for 3600 NM The final position of the aircraft is:
explanation: South 3 600 NM (60°) → Equator. East 3 600 NM = 60° d.long → 030°E. North 3 600 NM → 60°N. West 3 600 NM at 60°N = 7 200′ = 120° → 090°W. Final: 60°N 090°W.

question: The angle between the true great-circle track and the true rhumb-line track joining the following points: A (60° S 165° W) B (60° S 177° E), at the place of departure A, is:
explanation: Convergency = 18° × sin 60° = 15.6°; conversion angle (GC vs RL) = half = 7.8°.

question: The total length of the 30° Latitude is:
explanation: Length of a parallel = 21 600 × cos lat = 21 600 × cos 30° ≈ 18 706 NM.

question: In order to fly from position A (10° 00N, 030° 00W) to position B (30° 00N, 050° 00W), maintaining a constant true course, it is necessary to fly:

options.text: a straight line plotted on a Lambert chart.

explanation: A constant true course is by definition a rhumb line.

question: An aircraft departs from position A (04° 10 S 178° 22 W) and flies northward following the meridian for 2950 NM. It then flies westward along the parallel of latitude for 382 NM to position B. The coordinates of position B are?
A small circle:

options.text: has a plane parallel to the earth’s axis of rotation.
will also be a rhumb line.
has a plane that do not pass through the centre of the earth.

explanation: A small circle is a circle whose plane does not pass through the Earth's centre.

question: The following points are entered into an inertial navigation system (INS). WPT 1: 60° N 30° W WPT 2: 60° N 20° W WPT 3: 60° N 10° W The inertial navigation system is connected to the automatic pilot on route (1-2-3). The track change when passing WPT 2 will be approximately:
explanation: Each GC leg on 60°N changes track by the convergency 10 × sin 60° ≈ 9°; passing WPT 2 the track decreases by about 9°.

question: The great circle distance between position A (59° 34.1N 008° 08.4E) and B (30° 25.9N 171° 51.6W) is:
explanation: B's longitude is A's anti-meridian and the latitudes add to 90°, so the GC runs over the pole: (90 − 59.57) + (90 − 30.43) = 90° = 5 400 NM.

question: You are flying from A (30S 20E) to B (30S 20W). At what longitude will the GC track equal the RL track?
explanation: For two points on the same parallel the GC track equals the RL track at mid-longitude: 0° E/W.

question: An aircraft departs a point 0400N 17000W and flies 600 nm South, followed by 600 nm East, then 600 nm North, then 600 nm West. What is its final position?
An aircraft at latitude 10° South flies north at a GS of 890 km/HR. What will its latitude be after 1.5 HR?
You are flying from A (50N 10W) to B (58N 02E). At what longitude will the Great Circle track equal the Rhumb Line (RL) track between A and B:
explanation: GC and RL tracks are equal at about the mid-longitude: (10°W + 2°E)/2 = 4°W.

question: An approximate equation for calculating the convergency between two meridians is:

options.text: Convergency=60 x dlong x cos. lat.
Convergency= dlat x sin mean long
Convergency= dlong x sin mean lat.

explanation: Convergency = d.long × sin(mean latitude).

question: The great circle track X - Y measured at x is 319° , and Y 325° Consider the following statements:

options.text: Southern hemisphere, Rhumb line track is 322° .
Northern hemisphere, Rhumb line track is 313° .
Southern hemisphere, Rhumb line track is 331° .
Northern hemisphere, Rhumb line track is 322° .

explanation: The GC track increases (319° → 325°) while heading north-west. Westbound in the northern hemisphere a GC track decreases, so this must be the southern hemisphere. RL track = mean of initial and final ≈ 322°.

question: You are flying from A (30S 20E) to B (30S 20W). What is the final GC track?
explanation: Southern hemisphere, westbound: convergency = 40 × sin 30° = 20°. The GC starts at 270 − 10 = 260° and ends at 270 + 10 = 280°T.

question: The compression factor of the earth:

options.text: is so small that it may be ignored when making ordinary maps and charts.
makes the difference between the polar diameter and the equatorial diameter about 22 NM.

explanation: Compression ≈ 1/298 (≈ 1/300); the polar diameter is ≈ 43 km (≈ 22–23 NM) shorter, negligible for ordinary charts — all three are correct.

question: An aircraft passes position A (60° 00N 120° 00W) on route to position B (60° 00N 140° 30W). What is the great circle track on departure from A?
explanation: Westbound along 60°N, d.long 20.5°: convergency ≈ 17.8°, CA ≈ 8.9°. Northern hemisphere GC starts poleward of RL: 270 + 9 = 279°.

question: Given: Position A N60 W020, Position B N60 W021, Position C N59 W020. What are, respectively, the distances from A to B and from A to C?
explanation: A→B: 1° d.long at 60°N = 60 × cos 60° = 30 NM. A→C: 1° d.lat = 60 NM.

question: What is dlat from 30° 39S 20° 20E to 45° 23N 40° 40E:
explanation: Different hemispheres: add. 30°39′ + 45°23′ = 76°02′, direction north.

question: Given: Position A 45° N, ?° E Position B 45° N, 45° 15E Distance A-B=280 NM B is to the East of A Required: longitude of position A?

An aircraft is flying with aid of an inertial navigation system (INS) connected to the autopilot. The following two points have been entered in the INS computer: WPT 1: 60° N 030W WPT 2: 60° N 020° W When 025° W is passed the latitude shown on the display unit of the inertial navigation system will be:
explanation: Vertex of the GC between 60°N 030°W and 60°N 020°W is at 025°W: tan lat = tan 60°/cos 5° → 60°05.7′N.

question: An aeroplane flies from A (59° S 142° W) to B (61° S 148° W) with a TAS of 480 kt. The autopilot is engaged and coupled with an Inertial Navigation System in which AB track is active. On route AB, the true track:
explanation: INS flies the great circle: initial ≈ 233.7°T, final ≈ 238.9°T, so the track increases by ≈ 5° (≈ 6° × sin 60°).

question: Given: Position A is N00° E100° , Position B is 240° (T), 200 NM from A. What is the position of B?

An aircraft flies the following rhumb line tracks and distances from position 04° 00N 030° 00W: 600 NM South, then 600 NM East, then 600 NM North, then 600 NM West. The final position of the aircraft is:
Latitude may be defined as:

options.text: The distance from equator to a place on the surface of the earth.
The angle between the plane of the equator and the plane of the parallel of latitude.
The angular distance measured along a meridian from the equator to a parallel of the latitude, measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds and named North or South.
The displacement of a place from equator.

explanation: Latitude: angular distance along a meridian from the Equator, in degrees and minutes N or S.

question: An aircraft leaves ORLANDO FLORIDA (N 28° 32 W 081° 20) at 08:20 Z, GS 375. The ETA at TENERIFE. CANARIES (N 28° 32 W 016° 16) is:
explanation: Same latitude: RL along 28°32′N. D.long 65°04′ = 3 904′ × cos 28.5° ≈ 3 430 NM. Time ≈ 9 h 09 → 0820 + 0909 = 1729Z.

question: The distance between the parallels of latitude 17º 23S and 23º 59N is:
explanation: Opposite hemispheres: d.lat = 17°23′ + 23°59′ = 41°22′ = 2 482′ = 2 482 NM.

question: The automatic flight control system (AFCS) in an aircraft is coupled to the guidance outputs from an inertial navigation system (INS) and the aircraft is flying from waypoint 3 (35° S 050° W) to waypoint 4 (35° S 040° W). The initial track readout from waypoint 3 will be:
explanation: Southern hemisphere: the GC lies on the polar (south) side of the rhumb line, so eastbound it starts south of 090°: initial track > 090°.

question: Consider the following statements:

options.text: The exact length 1 minute of arc is shorter at high altitude than at sea level, when the arc is observed from the centre of the Earth.
In any position on the surface of the Earth, the length of 1 of arc East/West is equal to the length 1 minute of arc North/South in the same position on a perfect sphere.
The exact length 1 minute of arc varies a little from position to position because the Earth radius vary.

explanation: The Earth's radius of curvature varies, so 1′ of arc is not exactly constant. (At altitude 1′ of arc is longer, not shorter; E/W arcs along parallels are shorter.)

question: What is the Chlong (in degrees and minutes) from A (45N 16530E) to B (45N 15540W)?
An aircraft flies 448 nm along a parallel of latitude and the longitude changes by 8° 21. What is the latitude:
explanation: cos lat = departure / d.long = 448/501′ = 0.894 → lat ≈ 26°36′.

question: An aircraft at position 60GN 005° W tracks 090° (T) for 315 km. On completion of the flight the longitude will be:
Consider the following statements on departure:

options.text: As the difference of longitude increases, the departure is constant it the latitude is constant.
As the latitude increases, the departure between two meridians decreases.
Departure may be calculated using the equation: departure=Sin Lat. x sin Long.
Departure is independent of difference of longitude.

explanation: Departure = d.long × cos lat, so for the same two meridians departure decreases as latitude increases.

question: If an aeroplane was to circle around the Earth following parallel 60° N at a ground speed of 480 kt. In order to circle around the Earth along the equator in the same amount of time, it should fly at a ground speed of:
explanation: The Equator is twice the length of the 60° parallel → 2 × 480 = 960 kt.

question: The diameter of the Earth is approximately:
explanation: Earth's diameter ≈ 12 700 km (radius ≈ 6 370 km).

question: Using latitude and longitude for a place:

options.text: The distance from this place to another play may be easily calculated.
The location on the earth’s surface of this place is defined.
The direction from the place to any other place may be easily calculated.
Relative directions to another place may easily be calculated.

explanation: Latitude and longitude define a unique position on the Earth's surface.

question: The Rhumb line distance between A (53° 23N 001° 19W) and B (53° 23N 007° 47W) is:
A Parallel of Latitude is a:
explanation: Parallels (other than the Equator) are small circles.

question: An aircraft leaves 0° N/S 45° W and flies due south for 10 hours at a speed of 540 kts. What is its position?
explanation: 10 h × 540 kt = 5 400 NM = 90° of latitude: from the Equator due south → South Pole.

question: Consider the following statements on longitude.

options.text: Longitude is stated in degrees up to 360º .
The value of longitude will never exceed 90º .
The largest value of longitude is 180º .
The largest value of change of longitude is 90º .

explanation: Longitude runs 0–180° east or west; the maximum is 180°.

question: The latitude where the value of convergency is half the value of convergency at 60° N is:
explanation: Convergency ∝ sin lat: sin lat = ½ sin 60° = 0.433 → lat ≈ 25°39′.

question: An aircraft travels from point A to point B, using the autopilot connected to the aircrafts inertial system. The coordinates of A (45° S 010° W) and B (45° S 030° W) have been entered. The true course of the aircraft on its arrival at B, to the nearest degree, is:
explanation: Southern hemisphere westbound: GC initial ≈ 263°, final ≈ 277°T.

question: A great circle track joins position A (59° S 141° W) and B (61° S 148° W). What is the difference between the great circle track at A and B?
explanation: GC A → B: initial ≈ 237°, final ≈ 243°T — it increases by ≈ 6°.

question: Generally what line lies closer to the pole?

options.text: The rhumb line or great circle depending on the chart used.

explanation: The great circle always lies on the polar side of the rhumb line.

question: An approximate equation for calculation conversion angle is:

options.text: CA=0,5 x dlong x sin lat.
CA=dlong x sin Lat. x sin Long.
CA=0,5 x dlat x sin Lat.

explanation: Conversion angle ≈ ½ × d.long × sin(mean lat).

question: An aircraft at position 2700N 17000W travels 3000 km on a track of 180T, then 3000 km on a track of 090T, then 3000 km on a track of 000T, then 3000 km on a track of 270T. What is its final position?
A correct definition of longitude is:

options.text: The East-West distance between Greenwich and the place.
The arc at equator between the Greenwich meridian and the meridian of the place, measured in degrees, minutes and seconds, named East or West.
The angle between the Greenwich meridian and the meridian of the place.
The difference between the Greenwich meridian and the meridian of the place, measured at the centre of the earth.

explanation: Longitude: the arc of the Equator (or angle at the pole) between the prime meridian and the meridian of the place, 0–180° E or W.

question: Position A is at 70S 030W, position B is 70S 060E. What is the Great Circle track of B from A, measured at A?
explanation: Southern hemisphere eastbound, d.long 90°: convergency ≈ 84.6°, CA ≈ 42°. Initial GC = 090 + 42 ≈ 132°T (the GC bulges towards the South Pole).

question: What is the convergency at 5000N between the meridians 10500W and 14500W on the earth?
explanation: Convergency = 40 × sin 50° ≈ 30.6°.

question: A position P is located at 23º 45’ N, how many nautical miles is this point from the Equator?
explanation: 23°45′ = 1 425′ = 1 425 NM from the Equator.

question: What is the Rhumb Line track from A (4500N 01000W) to B (4830N 01500W)?
explanation: D.lat 3°30′ N, departure ≈ 5° × 60 × cos 46.75° ≈ 205 NM W → RL ≈ 315°T.

question: The rhumb-line distance between points A (60° 00N 002° 30E) and B (60° 00N 007° 30W) is:
You are flying from A (50N 10W) to B (58N 02E). If Inital Great Circle track is 047° T what is Final Great Circle track?
explanation: Final GC = initial + convergency = 047 + 12 × sin 54° ≈ 047 + 9.7 ≈ 057°T.

question: What is the Rhumb line (RL) direction from 45° N 14° 12W to 45° N 12° 48E?
explanation: Both points on 45°N, B east of A: the rhumb line is the parallel, 090°T.

question: The term departure used in navigation also have the following meaning:

options.text: Distance in direction East/West, given in nautical miles.
Angular distance along a parallel of latitude.

explanation: Departure is east–west distance in nautical miles.

question: The equator is located:

options.text: on the surface of the earth, being a circle whose plane is perpendicular to the axis of the earth and cutting through the centre of the earth.
on the surface of the earth and at right angles to the axis of rotation.
on the surface as a small circle, horizontal to the axis of rotation.
on the surface parallel to the magnetic equator.

explanation: The Equator is the great circle whose plane is perpendicular to the Earth's axis.

question: The poles on the surface of the earth may be defined as:

options.text: The points where the earth’s axis of rotation cuts the surface of the earth.
The points on the surface of the earth where all meridians intersect at right angles.
The points from where the distance to the equator is equal.
The points at which the vertical lines runs through the centre of the earth.

explanation: The geographic poles are where the Earth's axis of rotation meets the surface.

question: What is the distance in kilometres from 49° S 180° E/W to 58° S 180º E/W?
An Inertial Navigation System is used to navigate an aircraft from waypoint 1 (45° N 030° W) to waypoint 2 (45° N 020° W). The DSRTK readout approaching waypoint 2 will be:

options.text: 090° T or 270° T depending on the coupling selection.

explanation: INS flies the GC; eastbound in the northern hemisphere the GC track increases, so approaching WPT 2 it is more than 090°.

question: The circumference of the parallel of latitude at 60° N is approximately:
explanation: Length of a parallel = 21 600 × cos lat = 21 600 × 0.5 = 10 800 NM.

question: Assuming the Earth being a perfect sphere:

options.text: distances will vary, dependant on the latitude.
distances will vary, dependant on their directions.
a 1 minute arc measured on the surface of the Earth will be equally long wherever it is measured.

explanation: On a perfect sphere one minute of great-circle arc has the same length everywhere.

question: You are flying from A to B in the northern hemisphere. Your initial great circle track is 273° T and conversion angle is 6° . The rhumb line track from A to B is:
explanation: Northern hemisphere: the GC lies poleward of the RL, so westbound the GC starts north of the RL: RL = 273 − 6 = 267°T.

question: An aircraft at latitude 0220N tracks 180T for 685 kilometres. What is its latitude at the end of the flight?
Directions are stated:

options.text: As a reference direction and a number of degrees.
In degrees with reference to True North when plotted with reference to the latitude/longitude grid on a chart.
In degrees in a 360( system, starting out clockwise from the reference direction).

explanation: Directions are given as degrees (000–360, clockwise) from a stated reference (true, magnetic, grid); all three are correct.

question: The distance from A (S 27° 43 W 005° 15) to B(S 27° 43 E 018° 29):
A flight is to be made from A 49° S 180° E/W to B 58° S, 180° E/W. The distance in kilometres from A to B is approximately:
The rhumb line track between position A (45° 00N, 010° 00W) and position B (48° 30N, 015° 00W) is approximately:
A Great Circle passes through point A and point B. The initial track through A is 350º and the final track through B is 290º . The Convergence Angle is:
explanation: Convergency = change of GC direction between the two points: 290 − 350 = −60°.

question: An aircraft is at 10N and is flying South at 444 km/hour. After 3 hours the latitude is:

The automatic flight control system (AFCS) in an aircraft is coupled to the guidance outputs from an inertial navigation system (INS) and the aircraft is flying from waypoint No. 2 (60° 00S 070° 00W) to No. 3 (60° 00S 080° 00W). Comparing the initial track (° T) at 070° 00W and the final track (° T) at 080° 00W, the difference between them is that the initial track is approximately:
explanation: Southern hemisphere westbound along 60°S: GC initial ≈ 270 − 4.3 = 265.7°, final ≈ 274.3° → initial is ≈ 9° less.

question: The Great Circle bearing of B (70° S 060° E), from A (70° S 030° W), is approximately?
explanation: Southern hemisphere eastbound, d.long 90°: CA ≈ ½ × 90 × sin 70° ≈ 42° → GC ≈ 090 + 42 ≈ 133–135°T.

question: From position A (04° N 030° W) an aircraft flies 600 NM due south, then 600 NM due east, the 600 NM due north, then 600 NM due west. What is the aircrafts final position in relation to A?
explanation: The eastward leg (at 6°S) covers more longitude than the westward leg (at 4°N), so the aircraft ends due east of A.

question: Given: Great circle from P to Q measured at P=095° Southern hemisphere Conversion angle P - Q =7° What is the rhumb line track P - Q?
explanation: Southern hemisphere eastbound: the GC lies poleward (south) of the RL, so RL = 095 − 7 = 088°T.

question: An aircraft flies a rhumb line track from A (160° E) to B (170° W) at the same latitude in the Northern hemisphere. Its groundspeed is 300 knots and the flight takes three hours. The latitude of the aircraft is:
explanation: 30° d.long; 300 × 3 = 900 NM departure = 1 800 × cos lat → cos lat = 0.5 → 60°N.

question: An aircraft at position 6000N 00522W flies 165 km due East. What is the new position?
An aircraft flies a great circle track from 56° N 070° W to 62° N 110° E. The total distance travelled is:
explanation: 110°E is the anti-meridian of 070°W, so the GC goes over the pole: (90 − 56) + (90 − 62) = 62° = 3 720 NM.

question: An aircraft at latitude 02° 20N tracks 180° (T) for 685 nm. On completion of the flight the latitude will be:
What is the time required to travel along the parallel of latitude 60° N between meridians 010° E and 030° W at a groundspeed of 480 kt?
Parallels of latitude, except the equator are:

options.text: both Rhumb lines and Great circles.
are neither Rhumb lines nor Great circles.

explanation: Parallels other than the Equator are rhumb lines (constant direction 090/270) but not great circles.

question: Consider the following statements on the shape of the earth:

options.text: The diameters of the earth is the same at all latitudes.
The longest diameter is between the poles.
It is slightly flattened at the poles.
The diameter at the equator is about 60 NM longer than the diameter between the poles.

explanation: The Earth is slightly flattened at the poles (polar diameter ≈ 23 NM shorter).

question: Given: The coordinates of the heliport at Issy les Moulineaux are: N48° 50 E002° 16.5 The coordinates of the antipodes are:
explanation: Antipode: opposite latitude (48°50′S) and longitude 180° − 002°16.5′ = 177°43.5′W.

question: The initial great circle track from A (S 30° 45 E 045° 15) to B(S 30° 45 E 062° 38) is:
explanation: Southern hemisphere eastbound: GC initial ≈ 094.4°T (bulging towards the South Pole).

question: The automatic flight control system (AFCS) in an aircraft is coupled to the guidance outputs from an inertial navigation system (INS). The aircraft is flying between inserted waypoints No. 3 (55° 00N 020° 00W) and No.4 (55° 00N 030° 00W). With DSRTK/STS selected on the CDU, to the nearest whole degree, the initial track read- out from waypoint No. 3 will be:
explanation: Westbound along 55°N: GC initial ≈ 270 + ½ × 10 × sin 55° ≈ 274°T.

question: An aircraft leaves point A (75N 50W) and flies due North. At the North Pole if flies due south along the meridian of 65° 50E unit reaches 75N (point B). What is the total distance covered?
explanation: 75°N to the pole = 15° = 900 NM, and the same back down to 75°N: 1 800 NM.

question: Your position is 5833N 17400W. You fly exactly 6 nm eastwards. What is your new position?
Position A is located on the equator at longitude 130° 00E. Position B is located 100NM from A on a bearing of 225° (T). The coordinates of position B are:
explanation: 225° for 100 NM: d.lat = 70.7′ S, departure 70.7 NM W (at the Equator = 70.7′ d.long) → 01°11′S 128°49′E.

question: Calculate the dlat from N 001 15 E090 00 to S090 00:
explanation: From 01°15′N to 90°S: 91°15′ south.

question: Given: Waypoint 1 is 60S 030W, waypoint 2 is 60S 020W. What will be the approximate latitude on the display unit of an inertial navigation system at longitude 025W?
explanation: Southern hemisphere: the GC bulges towards the South Pole → 60°06′S at 025°W.

question: An aircraft takes off from 40° 20N 078° 38E and flies a Rhumb Line track of 090° . What is the longitude after it has flown 219 nm:
Given: value for the ellipticity of the Earth is 1/297. Earths semi-major axis, as measured at the equator, equals 6378.4 km. What is the semi-minor axis (km) of the earth at the axis of the Poles?
You are flying from A (30S 20E) to B (30S 20W). What is the RL track from A to B?
explanation: Both on 30°S, B west of A: the rhumb line is the parallel, 270°T.

question: The prime meridian is:

options.text: the meridian having the highest value of longitude.
the mid meridian on a chart.
the meridian running through Greenwich, England.

explanation: The prime meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich.

question: The earth may be referred to as:
explanation: The Earth is an oblate spheroid.

question: Consider the following statements on meridians:

options.text: Any two meridians will form a great circle.
The meridians are not of equal length.
The meridians are parallel only at equator.
Any two halves great circle will form a meridians.

explanation: A meridian and its anti-meridian together form a great circle.

question: The Initial Great Circle Track from A (S 27° 30 E 017° 45) to B (S 27° 30 E 029° 15) is:
explanation: Southern hemisphere eastbound, d.long 11.5° at 27.5°S → GC ≈ 092.65°T.

question: An aircraft is at position A (49° 10S 178° 22W). It flies due North for 2,950 NM and then due West for 382 NM to position B. Where is position B?
explanation: 2 950 NM north = 49°10′ → reaches the Equator. 382 NM west along the Equator = 6°22′ → 178°22′W − 6°22′ = 184°44′W = 175°16′E.

question: Calculate the dlong from N001 15 E090 00 to N001 15 E015 15:
explanation: From 090°E to 015°15′E: 74°45′ westwards.

question: Consider the following statements on rhumb lines:

options.text: Most rhumb lines will run as spirals from the one pole to another.
A rhumb line will never cross a great circle.
A rhumb line and a great circle will never have the same true direction for some distance.
The true direction of a rhumb line on northern hemisphere will increase in true direction, while on southern hemisphere it will decrease.

explanation: A rhumb line (other than meridians/parallels) spirals towards the poles (a loxodrome).

question: An aircraft starts at position 0410S 17822W and heads true north for 2950 nm, then turns 90 degrees left, and maintains a rhumb line track for 314 kilometres. What is its final position?
Consider the following statements on the great circle and the rhumb line running through the same two positions:

options.text: The rhumb line will in most cases be located closer to the equator than the great circle.
The great circle will in most cases be shorter of the two.
The great circle will in most cases run through an area of higher latitude than the rhumb line.

explanation: The RL lies nearer the Equator, the GC is shorter and passes through higher latitudes — all correct.

question: If you want to follow a constant true track value:

options.text: You must fly east/west or North/south.
You must fly a rhumb line.
You must fly a great circle.
You, in most cases, will also fly the shortest possible track.

explanation: A constant true track is a rhumb line.

question: In the northern hemisphere the rhumb line track from A to B is 230°, the convergency is 6° and the difference in longitude is 10°. What is the initial rhumb line track from B to A?
explanation: A rhumb line has the same direction everywhere, so the reverse rhumb-line track is simply the reciprocal: 230 − 180 = 050°. Convergency only affects great circles.

question: Departure (between two given meridians) is minimum at the:
explanation: Departure = d.long × cos lat, so it is greatest at the Equator and falls to zero at the poles.

question: Two aircraft start from the same position on the Equator. Aircraft A flies a track of 000°(T) for 5 400 NM, while aircraft B flies 090°(T) for 2 500 NM. On reaching their destinations, the bearing of A from B will be:
explanation: 5 400 NM = 90° of latitude, so A is at the North Pole. From anywhere, the North Pole lies due north: 000°(T).

question: An aircraft flies the following rhumb-line tracks and distances from 04°00′N 030°00′W: 700 NM south, 700 NM east, 700 NM north, 700 NM west. The final position is:
A great circle crosses the Equator on a true track of 062°T. What is the latitude of its northern vertex?
explanation: A great circle crossing the Equator at angle θ to the meridian reaches a maximum latitude of 90° − θ: 90 − 62 = 28°N (and 28°S on the other side).

question: What is the shortest distance in kilometres between Cairo (30°17′N 030°10′E) and Durban (29°48′S 030°10′E)?
What is the shortest distance in kilometres between San Francisco (38°N 123°W) and Dubai (25°N 057°E)?
explanation: 057°E is the anti-meridian of 123°W, so the great circle passes over the North Pole: (90 − 38) + (90 − 25) = 117° = 7 020 NM ≈ 13 001 km.

question: An aircraft at 00°00′N/S 163°27′W flies a track of 225°T for 70 NM. What is its new position?
explanation: 225° = SW. d.lat = 70 × cos 45° = 49.5′ S; departure 49.5 NM W = 49.5′ d.long at the Equator → 00°49′S 164°16′W.

question: An aircraft at 60°N 013°E flies 350 km due west. What is the new longitude?
An aircraft follows a great circle in the northern hemisphere. At a certain moment it is at the point where the great-circle direction is 270°(T). Continuing on the great circle:

options.text: the track angle will decrease and the latitude will decrease
the track angle will increase and the latitude will increase
the track angle will decrease and the latitude will increase
the track angle will remain constant

explanation: Direction 270° in the northern hemisphere means the aircraft is at the vertex (highest latitude). Continuing west, the GC turns south: track decreases (e.g. 265°) and latitude decreases.

question: On the Earth’s ellipsoid, one degree of latitude near the Equator is:
explanation: The Earth is flatter (larger radius of curvature) near the poles, so 1° of latitude is longest there (≈ 60.3 NM) and shortest near the Equator (≈ 59.7 NM).
